chapter_text:
CHAPTER 9 — भारतीयविज्ञानम् (BHARATIYA VIJNANAM)

Introduction — भारतीयविज्ञानम् किम्?

The Sanskrit word विज्ञानम् (vijnanam) is formed from वि (vi = special, deep) + ज्ञानम् (jnanam = knowledge). It therefore means "special, systematic knowledge" — that is, science. Long before modern laboratories existed, the sages and scholars of ancient India (प्राचीनभारतम्) observed nature carefully, measured the sky, healed the sick, worked with metals and numbers, and wrote down their findings in Sanskrit texts. This lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) celebrates भारतीयविज्ञानम् — the scientific tradition of India — through simple Sanskrit prose, a few famous public-domain verses, their शब्दार्थ (word meanings) and English translations, and a short grammar section drawn from the lesson.

प्रस्तावना (Prose introduction)

प्राचीनकाले भारतवर्षे विज्ञानस्य महती परम्परा आसीत्।
शब्दार्थ: प्राचीनकाले = in ancient times; भारतवर्षे = in India; विज्ञानस्य = of science; महती = great; परम्परा = tradition; आसीत् = was.
Translation: In ancient times there was a great tradition of science in India.

अस्माकं पूर्वजाः खगोलविज्ञाने, गणिते, आयुर्विज्ञाने, रसायनशास्त्रे, धातुविद्यायां च निपुणाः आसन्।
शब्दार्थ: अस्माकम् = our; पूर्वजाः = ancestors, forefathers; खगोलविज्ञाने = in astronomy; गणिते = in mathematics; आयुर्विज्ञाने = in medicine; रसायनशास्त्रे = in chemistry; धातुविद्यायाम् = in metallurgy; निपुणाः = skilled; आसन् = (they) were.
Translation: Our ancestors were skilled in astronomy, mathematics, medicine, chemistry and metallurgy.

ते स्वस्य ज्ञानं संस्कृतभाषायां ग्रन्थेषु अलिखन्।
शब्दार्थ: ते = they; स्वस्य = their own; ज्ञानम् = knowledge; संस्कृतभाषायाम् = in the Sanskrit language; ग्रन्थेषु = in books; अलिखन् = wrote (past tense).
Translation: They wrote their knowledge in books in the Sanskrit language.

(1) खगोलविज्ञानम् — Astronomy and आर्यभट

आर्यभटः प्राचीनः महान् खगोलशास्त्री गणितज्ञश्च आसीत्।
शब्दार्थ: आर्यभटः = Aryabhata; महान् = great; खगोलशास्त्री = astronomer; गणितज्ञः = mathematician; च = and.
Translation: Aryabhata was a great ancient astronomer and mathematician.

सः "आर्यभटीयम्" इति ग्रन्थम् अरचयत्।
शब्दार्थ: सः = he; आर्यभटीयम् = (the text) Aryabhatiya; ग्रन्थम् = book; अरचयत् = composed.
Translation: He composed the book called Aryabhatiya.

आर्यभटः अकथयत् — भूमिः स्वस्य अक्षे भ्रमति, आकाशं न भ्रमति।
शब्दार्थ: अकथयत् = said; भूमिः = the earth; अक्षे = on its axis; भ्रमति = rotates; आकाशम् = the sky; न = not.
Translation: Aryabhata said that the earth rotates on its own axis, and it is not the sky that moves.

सः ग्रहणस्य कारणम् अपि व्याख्यातवान् — छायया एव सूर्यग्रहणं चन्द्रग्रहणं च भवतः, न तु राहुणा।
शब्दार्थ: ग्रहणस्य = of the eclipse; कारणम् = cause; व्याख्यातवान् = explained; छायया = by shadow; सूर्यग्रहणम् = solar eclipse; चन्द्रग्रहणम् = lunar eclipse; भवतः = the two happen; न तु = and not; राहुणा = by (the demon) Rahu.
Translation: He also explained the cause of eclipses — solar and lunar eclipses happen because of shadows, not because of the demon Rahu.

(2) गणितम् — Mathematics: शून्यम् and the decimal system

भारतीयाः गणितज्ञाः शून्यस्य दशमलव-स्थानमान-पद्धतेः च आविष्कारं कृतवन्तः।
शब्दार्थ: भारतीयाः = Indian; गणितज्ञाः = mathematicians; शून्यस्य = of zero; दशमलव-स्थानमान-पद्धतेः = of the decimal place-value system; आविष्कारम् = invention, discovery; कृतवन्तः = made.
Translation: Indian mathematicians invented zero (शून्यम्) and the decimal place-value system.

शून्यम् एकः महान् आविष्कारः अस्ति; तेन विना अद्यतनं गणितं न सम्भवति।
शब्दार्थ: शून्यम् = zero; आविष्कारः = discovery; तेन विना = without it; अद्यतनम् = modern; गणितम् = mathematics; न सम्भवति = is not possible.
Translation: Zero is a great discovery; without it modern mathematics is not possible.

ब्रह्मगुप्तः शून्येन सह गणनस्य नियमान् अलिखत्।
शब्दार्थ: ब्रह्मगुप्तः = Brahmagupta; शून्येन सह = with zero; गणनस्य = of calculation; नियमान् = rules; अलिखत् = wrote.
Translation: Brahmagupta wrote the rules of calculation with zero.

भास्कराचार्यः "लीलावती" इति प्रसिद्धं गणितग्रन्थम् अरचयत्।
शब्दार्थ: भास्कराचार्यः = Bhaskaracharya; लीलावती = (the text) Lilavati; प्रसिद्धम् = famous; गणितग्रन्थम् = mathematics book; अरचयत् = composed.
Translation: Bhaskaracharya composed the famous mathematics book Lilavati.

एतत् भारतीयं गणितज्ञानम् अरबदेशद्वारा सर्वस्मै जगते अगच्छत्।
शब्दार्थ: एतत् = this; गणितज्ञानम् = mathematical knowledge; अरबदेशद्वारा = through the Arab lands; सर्वस्मै जगते = to the whole world; अगच्छत् = went.
Translation: This Indian mathematical knowledge spread to the whole world through the Arabs.

(3) आयुर्विज्ञानम् — Medicine: सुश्रुत and चरक

सुश्रुतः शल्यचिकित्सायाः पिता इति प्रसिद्धः।
शब्दार्थ: सुश्रुतः = Sushruta; शल्यचिकित्सायाः = of surgery; पिता = father; प्रसिद्धः = famous, well-known.
Translation: Sushruta is famous as the father of surgery.

सः "सुश्रुतसंहिता" इति ग्रन्थे शल्यक्रियायाः विधीन् अवर्णयत्; नासायाः पुनर्निर्माणम् अपि सः जानाति स्म।
शब्दार्थ: सुश्रुतसंहिता = the Sushruta-Samhita; शल्यक्रियायाः = of surgical operation; विधीन् = methods; अवर्णयत् = described; नासायाः = of the nose; पुनर्निर्माणम् = reconstruction (plastic surgery); जानाति स्म = used to know.
Translation: In the text Sushruta-Samhita he described the methods of surgery; he even knew the reconstruction of the nose (rhinoplasty).

चरकः आयुर्वेदस्य महान् आचार्यः आसीत्।
शब्दार्थ: चरकः = Charaka; आयुर्वेदस्य = of Ayurveda (medicine); आचार्यः = teacher, master.
Translation: Charaka was a great master of Ayurveda.

सः "चरकसंहिता" इति ग्रन्थे रोगाणां चिकित्सां वर्णयति।
शब्दार्थ: चरकसंहिता = the Charaka-Samhita; रोगाणाम् = of diseases; चिकित्साम् = treatment; वर्णयति = describes.
Translation: In the text Charaka-Samhita he describes the treatment of diseases.

आयुर्वेदः "आयुषः वेदः" अर्थात् जीवनस्य विज्ञानम् अस्ति।
शब्दार्थ: आयुः = life, lifespan; वेदः = knowledge, science; अर्थात् = that is; जीवनस्य = of life; विज्ञानम् = science.
Translation: Ayurveda means "the science of life" (आयुः + वेद).

(4) धातुविज्ञानम् — Metallurgy and the iron pillar

प्राचीनभारते धातुविद्या अपि उन्नता आसीत्।
शब्दार्थ: धातुविद्या = metallurgy, science of metals; उन्नता = advanced, developed.
Translation: In ancient India metallurgy too was advanced.

दिल्लीनगरे मेहरौली-प्रदेशे एकः लौहस्तम्भः तिष्ठति।
शब्दार्थ: दिल्लीनगरे = in the city of Delhi; मेहरौली-प्रदेशे = in the Mehrauli area; लौहस्तम्भः = iron pillar; तिष्ठति = stands.
Translation: In the Mehrauli area of Delhi stands an iron pillar.

सः स्तम्भः सहस्रवर्षेभ्यः अपि अधिकं कालं यावत् तिष्ठति, तथापि तत्र मलिनता (जङ्गम्) न भवति।
शब्दार्थ: सहस्रवर्षेभ्यः = for a thousand years; अधिकम् कालम् = a longer time; यावत् = up to; तथापि = even so; मलिनता / जङ्गम् = rust; न भवति = does not occur.
Translation: That pillar has stood for more than a thousand years, yet it does not rust.

एतत् प्राचीनभारतीयानां धातुविज्ञानस्य कौशलं दर्शयति।
शब्दार्थ: कौशलम् = skill, expertise; दर्शयति = shows.
Translation: This shows the metallurgical skill of the ancient Indians.

(5) अन्ये वैज्ञानिकाः — Other scientists

कणादः "अणुः" इति सूक्ष्मतमस्य कणस्य सिद्धान्तम् अवदत्।
शब्दार्थ: कणादः = Kanada; अणुः = atom; सूक्ष्मतमस्य = of the smallest; कणस्य = particle; सिद्धान्तम् = theory; अवदत् = stated.
Translation: Kanada put forward the theory of the अणु (atom), the smallest particle.

वराहमिहिरः "बृहत्संहिता" इति ग्रन्थे खगोलम् ऋतुविज्ञानं च अवर्णयत्।
शब्दार्थ: वराहमिहिरः = Varahamihira; बृहत्संहिता = the Brihat-Samhita; ऋतुविज्ञानम् = weather/season science.
Translation: Varahamihira in the Brihat-Samhita described astronomy and the science of weather.

नागार्जुनः रसायनशास्त्रे धातूनां संस्करणे च निपुणः आसीत्।
शब्दार्थ: नागार्जुनः = Nagarjuna; रसायनशास्त्रे = in chemistry; धातूनाम् = of metals; संस्करणे = in the processing/refining.
Translation: Nagarjuna was skilled in chemistry and in the processing of metals.

पद्यानि — Verses (with word meanings)

Verse 1 — आर्यभटस्य गणितम् (from the आर्यभटीयम्, गणितपादः; on the value of π):
चतुरधिकं शतमष्टगुणं द्वाषष्टिस्तथा सहस्राणाम् ।
अयुतद्वयविष्कम्भस्यासन्नो वृत्तपरिणाहः ॥
शब्दार्थ: चतुरधिकम् शतम् = a hundred increased by four (104); अष्टगुणम् = multiplied by eight (832); द्वाषष्टिः = sixty-two; तथा सहस्राणाम् = plus (that many) thousands → +62000 (= 62832); अयुतद्वय = two ayutas = 20000; विष्कम्भस्य = of the diameter; आसन्नः = approximate; वृत्तपरिणाहः = the circumference of a circle.
Translation: Add four to one hundred, multiply by eight, and add sixty-two thousand: this (62832) is the approximate circumference of a circle whose diameter is twenty thousand.
Note: 62832 ÷ 20000 = 3.1416, i.e. Aryabhata's value of π (पाई) correct to four decimal places — a remarkable ancient achievement.

Verse 2 — विद्यायाः महत्त्वम् (a famous public-domain subhashita):
नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुः नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः ।
नास्ति रागसमं दुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम् ॥
शब्दार्थ: नास्ति = there is not; विद्यासमम् = equal to knowledge; चक्षुः = eye; सत्यसमम् = equal to truth; तपः = penance; रागसमम् = equal to attachment; दुःखम् = sorrow; त्यागसमम् = equal to renunciation; सुखम् = happiness.
Translation: There is no eye like knowledge, no penance like truth, no sorrow like attachment, and no happiness like renunciation.
Moral: Knowledge (विद्या) is the truest eye — it lets us see the world rightly; science begins with this clear seeing.

Verse 3 — विद्याधनम् (a famous public-domain subhashita on the wealth of knowledge):
न चोरहार्यं न च राजहार्यं न भ्रातृभाज्यं न च भारकारि ।
व्यये कृते वर्धत एव नित्यं विद्याधनं सर्वधनप्रधानम् ॥
शब्दार्थ: न चोरहार्यम् = cannot be stolen by a thief; न राजहार्यम् = cannot be seized by a king; न भ्रातृभाज्यम् = cannot be divided among brothers; न भारकारि = is not a burden; व्यये कृते = when spent (used); वर्धते एव = only increases; नित्यम् = always; विद्याधनम् = the wealth of knowledge; सर्वधनप्रधानम् = the foremost of all wealth.
Translation: It cannot be stolen by a thief, seized by a king, divided among brothers, and it is no burden; the more it is spent the more it grows — the wealth of knowledge is the foremost of all wealth.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the lesson

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). When two sounds meet they often combine.
  • दीर्घ-सन्धि (long-vowel): विद्या + आलयः → विद्यालयः (आ + आ = आ) "school"; न + अस्ति → नास्ति (अ + अ = आ) "there is not".
  • गुण/वृद्धि-सन्धि: देव + ऋषिः → देवर्षिः (अ + ऋ = अर्); महा + आत्मा → महात्मा.
  • यण्-सन्धि: सु + आगतम् → स्वागतम् (उ + आ = व).
  • विसर्ग-सन्धि: आर्यभटः + अस्ति → आर्यभटोऽस्ति (ः + अ → ोऽ).
  Splitting a joined form back into its parts is called सन्धि-विच्छेद, e.g. नास्ति = न + अस्ति.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Sanskrit nouns change their ending to show their role. Examples from the lesson (a-stem आर्यभट / masculine, and others):
  • प्रथमा (nominative, subject): आर्यभटः "Aryabhata (did...)"; पूर्वजाः "ancestors" (plural).
  • द्वितीया (accusative, object): ग्रन्थम् "book (he wrote a BOOK)"; नियमान् "rules".
  • तृतीया (instrumental, by/with): छायया "BY a shadow"; अरबदेशद्वारा "through the Arabs".
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, from): सहस्रवर्षेभ्यः "from/for a thousand years".
  • षष्ठी (genitive, of): विज्ञानस्य "of science"; ग्रहणस्य "of the eclipse"; रोगाणाम् "of diseases".
  • सप्तमी (locative, in/at/on): भारतवर्षे "in India"; ग्रन्थेषु "in books"; अक्षे "on the axis".

(C) शब्दरूप (declension — worked example). The masculine a-stem noun वैज्ञानिक (scientist) in प्रथमा (nominative): एकवचन वैज्ञानिकः (one), द्विवचन वैज्ञानिकौ (two), बहुवचन वैज्ञानिकाः (many). The feminine word विद्या declines (प्रथमा): एकवचन विद्या, द्विवचन विद्ये, बहुवचन विद्याः.

(D) धातुरूप (verb conjugation — worked example, लट्लकार / present tense, प्रथमपुरुष). Root √भ्रम् (to rotate): भ्रमति (he/she/it rotates), भ्रमतः (the two rotate), भ्रमन्ति (they rotate) — as in "भूमिः भ्रमति". Root √अस् (to be): अस्ति (is), स्तः (the two are), सन्ति (they are). Root √कृ (to do): करोति, कुरुतः, कुर्वन्ति.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that विज्ञानम् (वि + ज्ञानम् = deep, systematic knowledge = science) flourished in ancient India. You met आर्यभट (earth's rotation, shadow-cause of eclipses, π ≈ 3.1416); you learned that Indians invented शून्यम् (zero) and the decimal system (ब्रह्मगुप्त, भास्कराचार्य, लीलावती); you read about सुश्रुत (father of surgery) and चरक (master of Ayurveda); and you saw the rust-free लौहस्तम्भ of Delhi, along with कणाद (अणु/atom), वराहमिहिर and नागार्जुन. You studied three verses with their शब्दार्थ, and drew grammar from the lesson: सन्धि (सन्धि-विच्छेद), the six विभक्ति, शब्दरूप (वैज्ञानिकः / वैज्ञानिकौ / वैज्ञानिकाः) and धातुरूप (भ्रमति / भ्रमतः / भ्रमन्ति). India's scientific tradition reminds us that curiosity and careful observation are the roots of all true knowledge.

topics.name: भारतीयविज्ञानस्य परिचयः — Introduction and Importance
topics.description: What विज्ञानम् (वि + ज्ञानम्, 'deep knowledge' = science) means, and how a great scientific tradition flourished in ancient India, recorded in Sanskrit texts across astronomy, mathematics, medicine, chemistry and metallurgy.

topics.name: खगोलविज्ञानम् — Astronomy and आर्यभट
topics.description: Aryabhata and his text Aryabhatiya: the earth rotating on its axis, the shadow-explanation of solar and lunar eclipses, and his remarkably accurate value of π (3.1416).

topics.name: गणितम् — Mathematics: Zero and the Decimal System
topics.description: India's invention of शून्यम् (zero) and the decimal place-value system, Brahmagupta's rules for zero, Bhaskaracharya's Lilavati, and how this knowledge spread to the world through the Arabs.

topics.name: आयुर्विज्ञानम् — Medicine: सुश्रुत and चरक
topics.description: Sushruta, the father of surgery, and his Sushruta-Samhita (including nose reconstruction); Charaka, master of Ayurveda, and the Charaka-Samhita; the meaning of आयुर्वेद as the science of life.

topics.name: धातुविज्ञानम् च अन्ये वैज्ञानिकाः — Metallurgy and Other Scientists

chapter_summary.title: भारतीयविज्ञानम् (Bharatiya Vijnanam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 9. It celebrates भारतीयविज्ञानम् — the scientific tradition of ancient India — covering astronomy (आर्यभट), mathematics (zero and the decimal system), medicine (सुश्रुत, चरक), metallurgy (the Delhi iron pillar) and other scientists, with verses on विद्या and simple grammar.

branches.label: खगोलम् — Astronomy
details: ग्रहणं छायया, न राहुणा (eclipses by shadow)

sections.heading: The scientific tradition of ancient India
bullets: विज्ञानम् = वि (deep/special) + ज्ञानम् (knowledge): systematic knowledge, i.e. science.
अस्माकं पूर्वजाः were skilled (निपुणाः) in astronomy, mathematics, medicine, chemistry and metallurgy.
They recorded their findings in Sanskrit texts (ग्रन्थेषु अलिखन्), giving India a long, documented scientific heritage.

sections.heading: Astronomy — आर्यभट
bullets: आर्यभटः composed आर्यभटीयम्, a landmark text of astronomy and mathematics.
He held that भूमिः स्वस्य अक्षे भ्रमति — the earth rotates on its axis — while the sky only appears to move.
He explained eclipses by shadows (छायया), not by the demon राहु, and computed π ≈ 3.1416 (62832 ÷ 20000).

sections.heading: Mathematics — zero and the decimal system
bullets: Indian mathematicians invented शून्यम् (zero) and the decimal place-value system (दशमलव-स्थानमान-पद्धतिः).
ब्रह्मगुप्तः wrote rules for calculating with zero; भास्कराचार्यः wrote the famous लीलावती.
This knowledge reached the whole world through the Arabs (अरबदेशद्वारा) — hence 'Hindu-Arabic numerals'.

sections.heading: Medicine and metallurgy
bullets: सुश्रुतः, the father of surgery, described surgical methods and even nose-reconstruction in the सुश्रुतसंहिता.
चरकः, master of आयुर्वेद ('science of life', आयुः + वेद), described disease and treatment in the चरकसंहिता.
The rust-free लौहस्तम्भ of Mehrauli, Delhi — standing over a thousand years — proves advanced धातुविज्ञान.

sections.heading: Verses and grammar
bullets: Aryabhata's verse 'चतुरधिकं शतम्...' encodes π; the subhashitas praise विद्या as the truest eye and the foremost wealth.
सन्धि: न + अस्ति = नास्ति; विद्या + आलयः = विद्यालयः; सु + आगतम् = स्वागतम्; splitting back = सन्धि-विच्छेद.
विभक्ति roles (भारतवर्षे 'in', विज्ञानस्य 'of', छायया 'by'), शब्दरूप (वैज्ञानिकः/-कौ/-काः) and धातुरूप (भ्रमति/भ्रमतः/भ्रमन्ति).

key_takeaways: विज्ञानम् (वि + ज्ञानम्) means science; ancient India had a great, well-documented scientific tradition.
आर्यभट taught that the earth rotates on its axis, explained eclipses by shadows, and computed π ≈ 3.1416.
India invented शून्यम् (zero) and the decimal place-value system, spread worldwide through the Arabs.
सुश्रुत is the father of surgery (सुश्रुतसंहिता) and चरक the master of Ayurveda (चरकसंहिता); आयुर्वेद = the science of life.
The rust-free iron pillar of Delhi proves the advanced धातुविज्ञान (metallurgy) of ancient India.
विद्या is praised as the truest eye and the foremost wealth — knowledge cannot be stolen and grows when shared.
Grammar from the lesson: सन्धि / सन्धि-विच्छेद, the six विभक्ति, शब्दरूप (वैज्ञानिकः) and धातुरूप (भ्रमति).

worksheet.title: Worksheet — भारतीयविज्ञानम् (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 9)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the lesson and verses where needed.

questions.question: Translate into simple English: 'आर्यभटः अकथयत् — भूमिः स्वस्य अक्षे भ्रमति, आकाशं न भ्रमति।'
questions.answer: Aryabhata said: the earth rotates on its own axis (अक्षे भ्रमति); it is not the sky (आकाशम्) that moves. This was a remarkably modern idea for its time.
questions.explanation: आर्यभट held that the apparent movement of the sky is really the earth's rotation.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: विज्ञानम्, पूर्वजाः, शून्यम्, लौहस्तम्भः, आसीत्.
questions.answer: विज्ञानम् = science / deep knowledge; पूर्वजाः = ancestors, forefathers; शून्यम् = zero; लौहस्तम्भः = iron pillar; आसीत् = (it) was.
questions.explanation: These words are drawn from the prose of the lesson.

questions.question: Who was सुश्रुत and why is he famous? Answer in one or two sentences.
questions.answer: सुश्रुत was an ancient Indian physician-surgeon, famous as the 'father of surgery' (शल्यचिकित्सायाः पिता). In his सुश्रुतसंहिता he described surgical methods, including reconstruction of the nose (rhinoplasty).
questions.explanation: Sushruta's Samhita is a foundational text of surgery.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) नास्ति (b) विद्यालयः.
questions.answer: (a) नास्ति = न + अस्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) विद्यालयः = विद्या + आलयः (आ + आ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and meaning-role of each word: भारतवर्षे, विज्ञानस्य, छायया.
questions.answer: भारतवर्षे = सप्तमी (locative) → 'in India'. विज्ञानस्य = षष्ठी (genitive) → 'of science'. छायया = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by a shadow'.
questions.explanation: सप्तमी shows place, षष्ठी shows possession, तृतीया shows means.

questions.question: Describe India's contribution to mathematics as told in this lesson (zero, the decimal system, Brahmagupta, Bhaskaracharya). Why is zero so important?
questions.answer: Indian mathematicians made two great gifts to the world: शून्यम् (zero) and the दशमलव-स्थानमान-पद्धतिः (decimal place-value system), in which the value of a digit depends on its position. ब्रह्मगुप्तः wrote the rules for calculating with zero, and भास्कराचार्यः composed the famous mathematics text लीलावती. This knowledge travelled to the rest of the world through the Arabs (अरबदेशद्वारा), which is why the numerals are called 'Hindu-Arabic'. Zero is especially important because it is both a number (nothing) and a place-holder; without it the place-value system, and therefore all modern arithmetic, algebra and computing, would be impossible.
questions.explanation: Cover zero, decimal system, the two mathematicians, transmission and the significance of zero.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) about Indian science, and give their English meaning.
questions.answer: 1. आर्यभटः महान् खगोलशास्त्री आसीत्। (Aryabhata was a great astronomer.) 2. भारतीयाः शून्यस्य आविष्कारं कृतवन्तः। (Indians invented zero.) 3. सुश्रुतः शल्यचिकित्सायाः पिता अस्ति। (Sushruta is the father of surgery.) Together they say that ancient Indians made great discoveries in astronomy, mathematics and medicine.
questions.explanation: Simple प्रथमा-subject sentences using the chapter's vocabulary and verbs आसीत्, कृतवन्तः, अस्ति.

questions.question: What is special about the iron pillar (लौहस्तम्भः) of Delhi, and what does it show?
questions.answer: The iron pillar in the Mehrauli area of Delhi has stood for more than a thousand years, yet it does not rust (जङ्गम् न भवति). It shows the advanced metallurgical skill (धातुविज्ञानस्य कौशलम्) of the ancient Indians.
questions.explanation: The rust-resistance proves sophisticated ancient metallurgy.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the verse line 'नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुः'. How does it relate to science?
questions.answer: It means 'there is no eye equal to knowledge' — विद्या (knowledge/learning) is the best eye because it lets us see and understand the world truly. Science (विज्ञानम्) grows from exactly this clear seeing: careful, knowledgeable observation of nature.
questions.explanation: Knowledge is likened to sight; science depends on such insight.

questions.question: What does the word विज्ञानम् mean, and name two fields in which ancient Indians excelled.
questions.answer: विज्ञानम् means science — deep, systematic knowledge (वि + ज्ञानम्). Ancient Indians excelled in many fields; two examples are खगोलविज्ञानम् (astronomy) and गणितम् (mathematics). (Others: आयुर्विज्ञानम् medicine, धातुविद्या metallurgy.)
questions.explanation: Definition of विज्ञानम् plus any two fields from the lesson.

______ अणुसिद्धान्तम् अवदत्। (name of sage)
शब्दार्थ: 'पूर्वजाः' = ______ (English).
शब्दार्थ: 'ग्रन्थः' = ______ (English, one word).
अनुवाद: 'शून्यम् महान् आविष्कारः अस्ति।' = Zero is a great ______.
What does the word विज्ञानम् mean, and how is it formed?
questions.answer: विज्ञानम् means science — deep, systematic knowledge. It is formed from वि (deep/special) + ज्ञानम् (knowledge).

questions.question: Name three fields in which ancient Indians were skilled, with one Sanskrit term each.
questions.answer: Three fields: astronomy (खगोलविज्ञानम्), mathematics (गणितम्) and medicine (आयुर्विज्ञानम्). Others include chemistry (रसायनशास्त्रम्) and metallurgy (धातुविद्या).
questions.explanation: The lesson lists five fields; any three are acceptable.

questions.question: What did आर्यभट say about the earth and the sky?
questions.answer: आर्यभट said that the earth (भूमिः) rotates on its own axis, and that the sky (आकाशम्) does not really move — its apparent motion is due to the earth's rotation.
questions.explanation: भूमिः अक्षे भ्रमति; आकाशं न भ्रमति.

questions.question: How did आर्यभट explain eclipses, and why was this important?
questions.answer: He explained that solar and lunar eclipses happen because of shadows (छाया) — the moon's or earth's shadow — and not because of the demon राहु. This was important because it replaced a superstition with a natural, scientific cause.

questions.question: Aryabhata's verse gives circumference 62832 for diameter 20000. Work out the value of π it implies.
questions.answer: π ≈ circumference ÷ diameter = 62832 ÷ 20000 = 3.1416. This matches the true value of π to four decimal places, showing Aryabhata's remarkable accuracy.

questions.question: What two great gifts did Indian mathematicians give to the world?
questions.answer: They gave शून्यम् (zero) and the दशमलव-स्थानमान-पद्धतिः (the decimal place-value system) — the foundation of modern numbers.
questions.explanation: Zero and the decimal place-value system.

questions.question: Who were ब्रह्मगुप्त and भास्कराचार्य, and what did each contribute?
questions.answer: ब्रह्मगुप्तः wrote the rules for calculating with zero. भास्कराचार्यः composed the famous mathematics text लीलावती. Both advanced Indian mathematics.

questions.question: How did Indian mathematical knowledge reach the rest of the world?
questions.answer: This knowledge spread from India to the whole world through the Arabs (अरबदेशद्वारा). That is why the numerals are known as 'Hindu-Arabic numerals'.

questions.question: Who was चरक and what is his text?
questions.answer: चरक was a great master (आचार्यः) of आयुर्वेद (Indian medicine). His text is the चरकसंहिता, which describes diseases and their treatment.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of आयुर्वेद and what सुश्रुत contributed to medicine.
questions.answer: आयुर्वेद means 'the science of life' (आयुः 'life' + वेद 'science'). सुश्रुत, the father of surgery, described surgical methods in the सुश्रुतसंहिता, including reconstruction of the nose (early plastic surgery).
questions.explanation: आयुर्वेद = science of life; Sushruta = surgery.

questions.question: What do the works of सुश्रुत and चरक together tell us about ancient India?
questions.answer: Together they show that ancient India had an advanced and well-organised system of medical science — both surgery (सुश्रुत) and internal medicine / Ayurveda (चरक) — recorded carefully in Sanskrit texts.
questions.explanation: Ancient Indian medicine was advanced in both surgery and Ayurveda.

questions.question: Where is the famous iron pillar, and what is remarkable about it?
questions.answer: The iron pillar stands in the Mehrauli area of Delhi. It is remarkable because it has stood for more than a thousand years yet does not rust.
questions.explanation: Mehrauli, Delhi; rust-free for over 1000 years.

questions.question: What does the rust-free iron pillar prove, and name two other ancient Indian scientists.
questions.answer: It proves the advanced metallurgical skill (धातुविज्ञानस्य कौशलम्) of ancient India. Two other scientists: कणादः (theory of the अणु/atom) and वराहमिहिरः (author of the बृहत्संहिता). Another is नागार्जुनः (chemistry).
questions.explanation: Advanced metallurgy; कणाद and वराहमिहिर (or नागार्जुन).

questions.question: What was कणाद's contribution to science?
questions.answer: कणादः proposed the theory of the अणु — the smallest, indivisible particle (an early idea of the atom). This shows deep thinking about the nature of matter.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: भ्रमति, छाया, ग्रन्थः, कौशलम्.
questions.answer: भ्रमति = rotates/moves; छाया = shadow; ग्रन्थः = book/text; कौशलम् = skill/expertise.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: आविष्कारः, निपुणः, रोगाणाम्, आचार्यः.
questions.answer: आविष्कारः = invention/discovery; निपुणः = skilled/expert; रोगाणाम् = of diseases; आचार्यः = teacher/master.

questions.question: Give the meaning of these verse words: चक्षुः, विद्यासमम्, विद्याधनम्, वृत्तपरिणाहः.
questions.answer: चक्षुः = eye; विद्यासमम् = equal to knowledge; विद्याधनम् = the wealth of knowledge; वृत्तपरिणाहः = the circumference of a circle.
questions.explanation: Word meanings from the three verses.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) विद्यालयः (b) स्वागतम्.
questions.answer: (a) विद्यालयः = विद्या + आलयः (आ + आ = आ). (b) स्वागतम् = सु + आगतम् (उ + आ = व, यण्-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting joined forms into their parts.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and role of: ग्रन्थम् (in 'ग्रन्थम् अरचयत्'), विज्ञानस्य, ग्रन्थेषु.
questions.answer: ग्रन्थम् = द्वितीया (accusative), the object → 'a book'. विज्ञानस्य = षष्ठी (genitive) → 'of science'. ग्रन्थेषु = सप्तमी (locative) → 'in books'.

questions.question: Give the धातुरूप (लट्, प्रथमपुरुष: singular, dual, plural) of √भ्रम्.
questions.answer: √भ्रम् (लट्, third person): एकवचन भ्रमति, द्विवचन भ्रमतः, बहुवचन भ्रमन्ति. (as in भूमिः भ्रमति).

questions.question: Translate: 'सुश्रुतः सुश्रुतसंहिता इति ग्रन्थे शल्यक्रियायाः विधीन् अवर्णयत्।'
questions.answer: Sushruta described the methods of surgery (शल्यक्रियायाः विधीन्) in the text called Sushruta-Samhita.

questions.question: Explain the message of the verse 'न चोरहार्यं... विद्याधनं सर्वधनप्रधानम्'.
questions.answer: The verse says the wealth of knowledge (विद्याधन) cannot be stolen by thieves, seized by kings or divided among brothers, and is no burden; the more it is used, the more it grows. Hence knowledge is the foremost of all wealth.
questions.explanation: Knowledge-wealth is safe, weightless and grows with use.

questions.question: Write a short paragraph on the scientific tradition of ancient India as described in the lesson.
questions.answer: Ancient India had a great tradition of science (विज्ञानम्, from वि + ज्ञानम्, 'deep knowledge'). Our ancestors (पूर्वजाः) were skilled (निपुणाः) in many fields: astronomy (खगोलविज्ञानम्), mathematics (गणितम्), medicine (आयुर्विज्ञानम्), chemistry (रसायनशास्त्रम्) and metallurgy (धातुविद्या). They observed nature carefully and wrote their findings in Sanskrit texts. This heritage — Aryabhata's astronomy, the invention of zero, Sushruta's and Charaka's medicine, and the rust-free iron pillar — shows that India valued careful observation and reasoned knowledge long ago.
questions.explanation: Definition of विज्ञानम् plus the range of fields and examples.

questions.question: Discuss आर्यभट's contributions to astronomy and mathematics, and why they were remarkable for their time.
questions.answer: आर्यभटः was a great ancient astronomer and mathematician who composed the आर्यभटीयम्. He held that the earth rotates on its own axis (भूमिः अक्षे भ्रमति) and that the sky only appears to move — a strikingly modern idea. He explained solar and lunar eclipses by shadows (छाया), rejecting the myth of the demon राहु and preferring a natural cause. In mathematics he gave a very accurate value of π: his verse 'चतुरधिकं शतम्...' yields 62832 ÷ 20000 = 3.1416, correct to four decimal places. These achievements were remarkable because he reached them through careful observation and calculation, without modern instruments, at a time when many cultures relied on myth.
questions.explanation: Cover rotation, eclipses, π, and why each was ahead of its time.

questions.question: Explain India's contribution to mathematics and why the invention of zero was so important.
questions.answer: Indian mathematicians invented शून्यम् (zero) and the decimal place-value system (दशमलव-स्थानमान-पद्धतिः), in which a digit's value depends on its position. ब्रह्मगुप्तः wrote the rules for calculating with zero, and भास्कराचार्यः composed the famous लीलावती. This knowledge spread to the world through the Arabs (अरबदेशद्वारा), giving us the 'Hindu-Arabic' numerals. Zero is so important because it is both a number and a place-holder: without it, the place-value system — and therefore all modern arithmetic, algebra, science and computing — would be impossible. In the lesson's words, तेन विना अद्यतनं गणितं न सम्भवति (without it modern mathematics is not possible).
questions.explanation: Zero, decimal system, the two mathematicians, transmission, and the significance of zero.

questions.question: Describe the contributions of सुश्रुत and चरक to Indian medicine.
questions.answer: सुश्रुतः is famous as the father of surgery (शल्यचिकित्सायाः पिता). In his text सुश्रुतसंहिता he described surgical methods, including the reconstruction of the nose (नासा-पुनर्निर्माणम्), an early form of plastic surgery. चरकः was a great master (आचार्यः) of आयुर्वेद, the 'science of life' (आयुः + वेद). In his text चरकसंहिता he described diseases (रोगाणाम्) and their treatment (चिकित्सा). Together they show that ancient India had an advanced, systematic medical science covering both surgery and internal medicine.
questions.explanation: Sushruta (surgery, Samhita, nose) and Charaka (Ayurveda, Samhita, treatment).

questions.question: Write about the iron pillar of Delhi and other ancient Indian scientists mentioned in the lesson.
questions.answer: In the Mehrauli area of Delhi stands a famous iron pillar (लौहस्तम्भः). It has stood for more than a thousand years, yet it does not rust (जङ्गम् न भवति). This proves the advanced metallurgical skill (धातुविज्ञानस्य कौशलम्) of ancient India. The lesson also mentions other scientists: कणादः, who proposed the theory of the अणु (atom, the smallest particle); वराहमिहिरः, author of the बृहत्संहिता on astronomy and weather; and नागार्जुनः, skilled in chemistry (रसायनशास्त्रम्) and the processing of metals. Together they show the breadth of ancient Indian science.
questions.explanation: Iron pillar plus कणाद, वराहमिहिर and नागार्जुन.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the verse 'नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुः...' and connect it to the study of science.
questions.answer: The verse says: there is no eye equal to knowledge (नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुः), no penance equal to truth (सत्यसमं तपः), no sorrow like attachment (रागसमं दुःखम्), and no happiness like renunciation (त्यागसमं सुखम्). The key line calls विद्या (knowledge) the truest 'eye', because it lets us see and understand the world correctly. This connects directly to science: विज्ञानम् grows from clear, knowledgeable seeing — careful observation of nature and honest reasoning. Just as an eye lets us see the physical world, knowledge lets us see how the world truly works.
questions.explanation: Meaning of each line, focus on विद्या as the eye, linked to scientific observation.

questions.question: Using examples from the lesson, explain सन्धि and विभक्ति, giving two examples of each.
questions.answer: सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where words meet. Examples: न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि) and सु + आगतम् = स्वागतम् (उ + आ = व, यण्-सन्धि). Splitting a joined form back is सन्धि-विच्छेद. विभक्ति is a noun's case ending, which shows its role in the sentence. Examples from the lesson: भारतवर्षे is सप्तमी (locative) meaning 'in India', and विज्ञानस्य is षष्ठी (genitive) meaning 'of science'. Another is छायया, तृतीया (instrumental), 'by a shadow'.
questions.explanation: Define both; give two sandhi and two vibhakti examples from the lesson.

questions.question: Write four simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) about Indian science, with English meanings.
questions.answer: 1. आर्यभटः आकाशं पश्यति स्म। (Aryabhata used to observe the sky.) 2. भारतीयाः शून्यम् आविष्कृतवन्तः। (Indians invented zero.) 3. सुश्रुतः शल्यचिकित्सां जानाति स्म। (Sushruta knew surgery.) 4. लौहस्तम्भः अद्यापि तिष्ठति। (The iron pillar still stands.) Together these sentences describe achievements of ancient Indian science in astronomy, mathematics, medicine and metallurgy.
questions.explanation: Simple correct sentences using chapter vocabulary and verbs.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'आर्यभटः प्राचीनः महान् खगोलशास्त्री आसीत्। सः अकथयत् — भूमिः स्वस्य अक्षे भ्रमति, आकाशं न भ्रमति। ग्रहणं छायया भवति, न राहुणा।'
Q: According to the passage, what two ideas did आर्यभट teach?
questions.answer: First, that the earth (भूमिः) rotates on its own axis while the sky (आकाशम्) does not really move. Second, that an eclipse (ग्रहणम्) is caused by a shadow (छाया), not by the demon राहु. Both are natural, scientific explanations.
questions.explanation: Earth's rotation and the shadow-cause of eclipses.

questions.question:
Read:
'आर्यभटः वृत्तस्य परिणाहं गणितवान् — विंशतिसहस्र-विष्कम्भस्य वृत्तस्य परिणाहः द्वाषष्टिसहस्र-अष्टशत-द्वात्रिंशत् (62832) प्रायः भवति।'
Q: What value of π does this give, and what does it show?
questions.answer: π ≈ 62832 ÷ 20000 = 3.1416. This shows that आर्यभट calculated π correct to four decimal places, a remarkably accurate result for the ancient world.

questions.question:
Read:
'भारतीयाः गणितज्ञाः शून्यस्य दशमलव-पद्धतेः च आविष्कारं कृतवन्तः। एतत् ज्ञानम् अरबदेशद्वारा सर्वस्मै जगते अगच्छत्।'
Q: What did Indian mathematicians invent, and how did it reach the world?
questions.answer: They invented शून्यम् (zero) and the दशमलव (decimal) place-value system. This knowledge reached the whole world through the Arabs (अरबदेशद्वारा) — which is why the numerals are called 'Hindu-Arabic'.
questions.explanation: Zero + decimal system; spread via the Arabs.

questions.question:
Read:
'शून्यम् एकः महान् आविष्कारः अस्ति; तेन विना अद्यतनं गणितं न सम्भवति।'
Q: Why does the passage call zero a great invention?
questions.answer: Because without zero, modern mathematics is not possible (तेन विना अद्यतनं गणितं न सम्भवति). Zero acts as both a number and a place-holder, making the whole decimal system — and modern arithmetic, algebra and computing — work.
questions.explanation: Zero is essential to the place-value system and all modern mathematics.

questions.question:
Read:
'सुश्रुतः शल्यचिकित्सायाः पिता। सः सुश्रुतसंहितायां शल्यक्रियायाः विधीन् अवर्णयत्; नासायाः पुनर्निर्माणम् अपि सः जानाति स्म।'
Q: What does this passage tell us about सुश्रुत?
questions.answer: It tells us that सुश्रुत was the father of surgery, that he described surgical methods in the सुश्रुतसंहिता, and that he even knew how to reconstruct the nose (नासा-पुनर्निर्माणम्) — an early form of plastic surgery.
questions.explanation: Father of surgery; described methods; knew rhinoplasty.

questions.question:
Read:
'चरकः आयुर्वेदस्य महान् आचार्यः आसीत्। सः चरकसंहितायां रोगाणां चिकित्सां वर्णयति। आयुर्वेदः जीवनस्य विज्ञानम् अस्ति।'
Q: Who was चरक and what is आयुर्वेद?
questions.answer: चरक was a great master (आचार्यः) of आयुर्वेद, who described the treatment of diseases in the चरकसंहिता. आयुर्वेद means 'the science of life' (आयुः + वेद) — the ancient Indian system of medicine.
questions.explanation: Charaka = master of Ayurveda; Ayurveda = science of life.

questions.question:
Read:
'दिल्लीनगरे मेहरौली-प्रदेशे एकः लौहस्तम्भः तिष्ठति। सः सहस्रवर्षेभ्यः अपि अधिकं कालं तिष्ठति, तथापि तत्र जङ्गम् न भवति।'
Q: What is remarkable about this pillar, and what does it prove?
questions.answer: The pillar has stood for more than a thousand years, yet it does not rust (जङ्गम् न भवति). This is remarkable and proves the advanced metallurgical skill (धातुविज्ञानस्य कौशलम्) of ancient India.
questions.explanation: Rust-free for over 1000 years; proves advanced metallurgy.

questions.question:
Read:
'कणादः अणुसिद्धान्तम् अवदत्। वराहमिहिरः बृहत्संहितायां खगोलम् अवर्णयत्। नागार्जुनः रसायनशास्त्रे निपुणः आसीत्।'
Q: Match each scientist to his field.
questions.answer: कणादः — the theory of the अणु (atom); वराहमिहिरः — astronomy (author of the बृहत्संहिता); नागार्जुनः — chemistry (रसायनशास्त्रम्). Each represents a different branch of ancient Indian science.

questions.question:
Read the verse:
'नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुः नास्ति सत्यसमं तपः।'
Q: Translate the line and explain its meaning.
questions.answer: Translation: There is no eye equal to knowledge, and no penance equal to truth. Meaning: विद्या (knowledge) is the best 'eye' because it lets us see the world truly, and truthfulness is the greatest तपस् (discipline). Knowledge and truth are supreme values.
questions.explanation: Knowledge is the truest eye; truth the greatest penance.

questions.question:
Read:
'एतत् सर्वं दर्शयति यत् प्राचीनभारते विज्ञानस्य महती परम्परा आसीत्। अस्माभिः अपि विज्ञाने रुचिः धारणीया।'
Q: What conclusion and lesson does this passage draw for students today?
questions.answer: It concludes that ancient India had a great tradition of science (विज्ञानस्य महती परम्परा). The lesson for students is that we too should keep an interest in science (विज्ञाने रुचिः धारणीया) — learning from our heritage of curiosity, observation and reasoning.
questions.explanation: Conclusion: great scientific heritage; lesson: cultivate interest in science.
